segments.en: A young man stands on the rim of a pale stone arch high above an emerald river. The crowd holds its breath, he spreads his arms, and he dives. This is the Old Bridge of Mostar, and this is Bosnia and Herzegovina.
segments.bs: Mladić stoji na rubu blijedog kamenog luka, visoko iznad smaragdne rijeke. Okupljeni zadržavaju dah, on raširi ruke i skoči. Ovo je Stari most u Mostaru, a ovo je Bosna i Hercegovina.

segments.en: Ottoman builders raised the bridge more than four centuries ago, and early this century it was lovingly rebuilt using the old methods. Diving from it is a tradition the town has kept for generations.
segments.bs: Most su prije više od četiri stoljeća podigli osmanski graditelji, a početkom ovog stoljeća s ljubavlju je obnovljen starim tehnikama. Skokovi s mosta tradicija su koju grad čuva generacijama.

segments.en: The country is shaped a little like a heart. Bosnia is the green, forested north, and Herzegovina the sunnier, rockier south, where figs and grapes ripen in the heat.
segments.bs: Zemlja pomalo podsjeća na srce. Bosna je zeleni, šumoviti sjever, a Hercegovina sunčaniji, kamenitiji jug, gdje na vrućini sazrijevaju smokve i grožđe.

segments.en: In Sarajevo, the capital, wander through Baščaršija, the old bazaar, where coppersmiths tap at trays and pigeons gather around a wooden fountain. In one short stroll you can pass a mosque, an Orthodox church, a Catholic cathedral and a synagogue.
segments.bs: U Sarajevu, glavnom gradu, prošetaj Baščaršijom, starom čaršijom, gdje kazandžije kuckaju po tepsijama, a golubovi se skupljaju oko drvene česme Sebilj. U samo jednoj kratkoj šetnji proći ćeš pored džamije, pravoslavne crkve, katoličke katedrale i sinagoge.

segments.en: Here coffee is never rushed. It arrives in a small copper pot with tiny cups, a cube of sugar and a piece of rahat lokum. Sipping slowly and chatting for an hour is all part of the ritual.
segments.bs: Ovdje se kafa nikad ne pije na brzinu. Stiže u maloj bakrenoj džezvi, s fildžanima, kockom šećera i komadićem rahat-lokuma. Polagano pijuckanje i sat vremena razgovora dio su tog obreda.

segments.en: There is even a word for that unhurried pleasure: ćejf. Doing something with ćejf means doing it just the way you like it, in your own good time.
segments.bs: Postoji čak i riječ za to neužurbano zadovoljstvo: ćejf. Raditi nešto s ćejfom znači raditi to baš onako kako voliš, bez imalo žurbe.

segments.en: Hungry? Order ćevapi, little grilled rolls of minced meat tucked into warm, soft flatbread called somun, with chopped raw onion. And remember, only the meat pie is called burek. With cheese it becomes sirnica, with spinach zeljanica.
segments.bs: Ogladnio si? Naruči ćevape, male komade mljevenog mesa s roštilja u toplom, mekom somunu, uz nasjeckani luk. I zapamti: samo pita s mesom zove se burek. Sa sirom je sirnica, a sa zeljem zeljanica.

segments.en: In the evenings, listen for sevdalinka, old love songs full of longing, sung slowly to an accordion or a long-necked saz. People say sevdah is a sweet sadness you feel in the heart.
segments.bs: Uvečer osluhni sevdalinku, stare ljubavne pjesme pune čežnje, koje se pjevaju polako uz harmoniku ili saz dugog vrata. Kažu da je sevdah slatka tuga koju osjećaš u srcu.

segments.en: Across the hills stand stećci, medieval tombstones carved with spirals, hunters and dancers. Neighbouring lands have them too, but many of the finest are right here.
segments.bs: Po brdima stoje stećci, srednjovjekovni nadgrobni spomenici ukrašeni spiralama, lovcima i plesačima. Ima ih i u susjednim zemljama, ali mnogi od najljepših nalaze se upravo ovdje.

segments.en: The rivers are unforgettable. In Jajce a waterfall tumbles through the middle of town, and at Kravica water spills over a wide rocky amphitheatre into natural pools.
segments.bs: Rijeke se ne zaboravljaju. U Jajcu vodopad pada usred samog grada, a na Kravici se voda preliva preko širokog kamenog amfiteatra u prirodne bazene.

segments.en: In winter the mountains above Sarajevo fill with skiers. The city hosted the Winter Olympic Games in nineteen eighty-four, and locals still remember it with pride.
segments.bs: Zimi se planine iznad Sarajeva pune skijaša. Grad je bio domaćin Zimskih olimpijskih igara hiljadu devetsto osamdeset četvrte, i Sarajlije se toga i danas s ponosom sjećaju.

segments.en: People speak Bosnian, Croatian and Serbian, close cousins written in both Latin and Cyrillic letters. A warm merhaba or dobar dan opens many doors, and a guest is always offered something to eat.
segments.bs: Ovdje se govori bosanski, hrvatski i srpski, bliski jezici koji se pišu i latinicom i ćirilicom. Toplo merhaba ili dobar dan otvara mnoga vrata, a gostu se uvijek ponudi nešto za jelo.

segments.en: Now follow the Neretva south as it hurries toward the Adriatic, and soon you will cross into Croatia, where the sea is waiting.
segments.bs: Sada prati Neretvu na jug dok žuri prema Jadranu, i uskoro ćeš preći u Hrvatsku, gdje te čeka more.
